PROBLEM: A compensating controller removes the physical symptom of a fault from the vehicle response, so a monitor that reads the response sees nominal behaviour while the fault persists.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: rate-loop and integral compensation; control allocation; autopilot trim
WHO_HAS_IT: every closed-loop vehicle with physical-response monitors
WHY_IT_MATTERS: masked faults surface only when authority runs out (L057, L059); XSYS-001 negative control 55/55 wrong (L069)
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: closed-loop FDI and fault masking (L002, L021); integrated control and diagnosis since 1988 (L003, L004); detectability-performance trade-off (L014); masking assumptions in model-based diagnosis (L020)
WHAT_REMAINS: nothing at problem level: the mechanism, its trade-off and its remedy (read the control signal or a command-driven plant residual) are textbook

PROBLEM: After a compensating or reconfiguring action (gain change, allocation change, motor removal, mode change), runtime monitors do not record which of their evidence relations the action invalidated and continue to apply them.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: vibration-resistant gains; motor removal and restore; mode reversion
WHO_HAS_IT: modular autopilots and autonomy stacks whose monitors are written per module
WHY_IT_MATTERS: the fielded vibration check clears itself using the same detector under the compensated controller (L066); XSYS-001 shows the error size when a relation is used after compensation (L069); autopilot masking upsets (L057, L059)
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: mode-dependent and mode-sequence ARRs in hybrid diagnosis (L017); command-conditioned mode identification, flown on DS1 (L012); ModelPlex model monitors conditioned on the action (L035); FRET mode scopes (L037); integration issues in active FTC (L004)
WHAT_REMAINS: theory already treats interventions as modes; the residual is making modular stacks declare their interventions to monitors and giving each monitor mode-scoped validity; engineering

PROBLEM: Runtime diagnostic evidence is validated by time since fault onset, whereas its validity actually depends on the control and action history applied since onset.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: different controllers or manoeuvres after the same onset
WHY_IT_MATTERS: two identical timestamps can carry different evidence meaning under different controllers
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: input-dependent nonlinear observability (L018); persistent-excitation conditions for multiplicative faults (L015); mode-sequence ARRs (L017); monitors conditioned on the executed action (L035); set-based diagnosis computed for the applied input (L007); the dual effect (L013)
WHAT_REMAINS: nothing at problem level: model-based residuals condition on the input by construction, and input-dependent detectability is standard

PROBLEM: A monitor that triggers an intervention does not account for how that intervention will change its own future evidence, so its later conclusions are biased by its own action.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: failsafe escalation that resets or switches the estimator; alert-triggered avoidance
WHO_HAS_IT: monitors with escalation ladders; runtime-assurance switches
WHY_IT_MATTERS: fielded escalation keeps counting on post-intervention evidence (L066); model-triggered actions make effective monitors look wrong (L025)
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: dual control and unified active detection and control (L006, L013); belief-space shielding with active information gathering (L034); safe active diagnosis (L009); monitoring under performativity (L026)
WHAT_REMAINS: the theory closes the loop (dual control, POMDP belief planning); fielded runtime assurance does not, and applying the theory there is known-method application

PROBLEM: Estimator interventions (reset, sensor exclusion, lane switch, covariance change, re-classification, validity hold) change the semantics of the evidence stream that downstream monitors and assurance arguments consume, without those consumers accounting for it.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: EKF lane switch; yaw or position reset; GNSS exclusion; object re-classification; memorisation period
WHO_HAS_IT: navigation and perception stacks with redundancy management
WHY_IT_MATTERS: MH124 (L055), QF72 (L061), Uber ATG (L056), SOHO (L054) all involve an estimator or redundancy-management action changing what later data meant
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: ARAIM protection levels after exclusion (L040); Kalman-filter integrity with residual history (L041); fielded reset counters, lane-switch reset data and switch hold-off (L063, L064, L065)
WHAT_REMAINS: the integrity mathematics exists for navigation; fielded stacks propagate resets to controllers but, in the files read, not to every monitor (L068); engineering

PROBLEM: Safety-preserving actions chosen by a planner or controller remove the excitation that would distinguish competing fault hypotheses, and the assurance layer does not register that the resulting ambiguity is caused by its own action rather than by health.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: gentle trajectory after suspected propulsion loss; hover hold; reduced manoeuvre envelope
WHO_HAS_IT: autonomous vehicles that restrict manoeuvres after a suspected fault
WHY_IT_MATTERS: safer but less diagnosable; persistent ambiguity can be misread as exoneration (L069); planners tend to move into unobservable subspaces (L018)
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: s-FEAST safe active fault estimation with probabilistic state constraints (L009); safe real-time active model discrimination for quadrotor and fighter-jet models (L008); safety-constrained guaranteed active diagnosis (L007); safe diagnosability and active safe diagnosis (L010); unified active detection and control (L006); observability-aware planning (L018)
WHAT_REMAINS: passive accounting of diagnosability lost through actions chosen by other modules; a likelihood or set-based diagnoser handles this automatically, so what remains is scale and speed, already addressed by L008 and L009

PROBLEM: Safety-preserving actions suppress fault symptoms and thereby generate evidence that falsely exonerates the physical cause.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: compensation that returns the response to nominal
WHO_HAS_IT: monitors that treat a nominal response as proof of health
WHY_IT_MATTERS: XSYS-001: after compensation the dynamics witness refuted the physical cause in 55/55 trials (L069)
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: explicit no-fault-masking and exoneration assumptions in model-based diagnosis (L020); autopilot masking accidents (L057, L059); passive fault tolerance hiding faults until redundancy is exhausted (L051); control-signal-based closed-loop detection (L021, L002)
WHAT_REMAINS: nothing at problem level: do not exonerate on a channel the loop regulates; read the control effort instead (as W_CTRL did, L070)

PROBLEM: Monitors do not represent why an observation exists or which autonomy actions influenced it, so evidence carries no provenance through the autonomy loop.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: any controller, estimator or planner action upstream of a measurement
WHY_IT_MATTERS: TMI indicator showed the command, not the state (L052); Uber ATG discarded track history on re-classification (L056)
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: decision provenance (L043); ROS message provenance (L044); reset counters and deltas published to consumers (L063, L064); command history in model-based mode identification (L012)
WHAT_REMAINS: capturing action provenance is data-flow engineering; using it is P02 or P05

PROBLEM: In-service assurance evidence (safety performance indicators, monitor alarm statistics, fleet outcome data) is generated under the system's own interventions, so the outcomes that would validate or refute a monitor are prevented by the actions it triggers, and assurance arguments treat that data as if it were observational.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: alert-triggered avoidance; runtime-assurance switch; operator takeover
WHO_HAS_IT: operators maintaining field safety cases for autonomous aircraft
WHY_IT_MATTERS: effective interventions make monitors look wrong (L025); outcomes are selectively observed (L027)
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: selective labels (L027); performative monitoring (L026); inference on adaptively collected data (L023); g-methods (L022); counterfactual simulation of takeovers (L039); SPI argument patterns and meta-SPIs (L038)
WHAT_REMAINS: no directly matching work was identified in the searched sources for aerospace SPIs or runtime-assurance monitors; the formal problem and its tools are established elsewhere, and deterministic policies push identification towards simulation, as L039 already does

PROBLEM: Adaptive control or adaptive estimation absorbs a fault into its nominal model, and good regulation removes the excitation needed to identify it.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: adaptive gains; noise-covariance adaptation; hover-thrust estimation
WHO_HAS_IT: adaptive flight control and adaptive filters
WHY_IT_MATTERS: the reference that monitors compare against moves with the fault
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: loss of persistent excitation and parameter drift (L016); adaptive controllers masking fault signatures (L002); adaptive Kalman filters under faults (L042); the internal null-arm measurement (L071)

PROBLEM: A runtime-assurance switch or safety shield changes the data that learning, adaptation or monitoring components receive afterwards, biasing their updates and validation.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: Simplex switch to the backup controller; shield veto; recovery policy
WHY_IT_MATTERS: validation data for the advanced controller is censored where it matters most
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: shield and recovery-intervention bias with corrections (L033); runtime assurance and distribution-shift monitoring (L032); belief-space shielding (L034); performative prediction (L024)
WHAT_REMAINS: corrections exist for learning; the monitoring side is the same problem as P09

PROBLEM: Monitor evidence semantics are not invariant to the autonomy policy, so a monitor calibrated under one controller or planner misreads evidence under another.
EXAMPLE_INTERVENTIONS: controller retune; new planner; new flight mode
WHY_IT_MATTERS: closed-loop response envelopes move with the controller (L070)
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: the Lucas critique and structural invariance (L028); invariant causal prediction (L030); direct closed-loop identification (L001); monitors conditioned on the executed action (L035); command-driven residuals (L021)
WHAT_REMAINS: nothing at problem level: invariance comes from conditioning on the actual input with a plant model; where no plant model exists the problem is P09 or performative prediction (L024)

PROBLEM: There is no unified cross-domain theory of evidence generated under an autonomous system's own interventions for assurance purposes.
WHO_HAS_IT: assurance researchers working across control, statistics and machine learning
WHY_IT_MATTERS: the same phenomenon is solved separately in each field
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: the g-formula for sequential interventions (L022); the dual effect and POMDP belief dynamics (L013, L034); performative prediction (L024); the Lucas critique (L028)
WHAT_REMAINS: nothing substantive: the interventional distribution of evidence given the action history is the common formalism already; a unifying framework would rename it
